newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland on course to meet EMU criteria - Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Ireland on course to meet EMU criteria - Central Bank.

text.p: The Irish Central Bank said on Wednesday that Ireland was broadly on course to meet the Maastricht criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
But the bank warned in its quarterly bulletin that Irish fiscal policy should not be expansionary.
"The present buoyant disposition of the economy does not warrant an expansionary fiscal stance which could only serve to increase inflationary dangers which may already be present," the bank said.
It said that tax reductions should at least be matched by restraints on public spending within the desired fiscal stance.
"Looking further ahead, there is a need to plan for the requirements of the public finance stability pact in EMU and the future reduction of EU structural funds," the bank said in the bulletin.
On qualifying for EMU, the bank said there needed to be ongoing concern about satisfying the price stability criterion and warned that the risk of higher inflation should not be understated.
It noted that although the most recent headline Irish inflation rate was low at 1.5 percent, the rate used for measuring intra-EU comparisons was 2.2 percent.
This compares with an average rate of 1.0 percent for the three lowest inflation countries in the European Union, the bank said.
"Economic growth has been exceptionally strong and the data would seem to indicate that there is now only a small gap between the economy's potential output and actual output," it said.
